question: Calcineurin inhibitors such as ciclosporin and tacrolimus prevent T-cell activation primarily by blocking interleukin-2 production.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Calcineurin inhibitors — ciclosporin and tacrolimus — do act by blocking IL-2 production. Calcineurin is required to activate the transcription factor NFAT, which drives IL-2 gene expression; blocking calcineurin suppresses T-cell activation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Calcineurin inhibitors inhibit the calcineurin-NFAT pathway, thereby blocking transcription of IL-2 and other cytokines required for T-cell proliferation and graft rejection.
